title: De Administrando Imperio
fact_summary: A Byzantine handbook on foreign peoples, compiled for Emperor Constantine VII's son around 950. Its chapter 38 is one of the oldest accounts of Hungarian early history.

claims.text: It was compiled between 948 and 952 under Emperor Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos (reigned 944–959) for his son Romanos.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study states it.

claims.text: Chapter 38 is about the origin and history of the Hungarians before they settled in the Carpathian Basin.
The oldest surviving copy is a manuscript in Paris, Codex Parisinus Graecus 2009.
That Paris copy was made at the end of the 11th century.

held_by.who: The earlier dating, as reported by Tóth (2015)

claims.certainty_reason: Tóth reports a more recent dating to the 12th century.

claims.text: That Paris copy was made in the 12th century.

held_by.who: More recent scholarship, as reported by Tóth (2015)

claims.certainty_reason: Who proposed it is not named here yet.

contradictions.what_differs: When the oldest copy was written: late 11th century or 12th century.

open_questions.text: The Greek text itself has not been opened for this map. A free copy of the Moravcsik and Jenkins edition would let chapter 38 be checked directly.
